posts.title: mc² + IGNITE: strengthening the startup ecosystem
posts.excerpt: India's flagship energy innovation accelerator came to IIT Guwahati — bringing startups, students, PSUs, investors and policymakers onto one platform, with 1,500+ participants and 100+ startups.
posts.author: IITG-TIC with Oil India Limited and the MC² Foundation

coverImage.alt: Dignitaries on stage at the mc² + IGNITE accelerator.

body.text: mc² + IGNITE — India’s flagship energy innovation accelerator — concluded at IIT Guwahati, bringing startups, students, entrepreneurs, policymakers, PSUs, industry leaders, investors and academia onto a single platform. The IITG Technology Incubation Centre (IITG-TIC) and IIT Guwahati were partners in the initiative, connecting innovation, academia, industry and entrepreneurship.
A vision for the ecosystem

The Hon’ble Chief Minister of Assam, Dr Himanta Biswa Sarma, spoke to the potential of entrepreneurship and technology-led innovation, and to the need for a stronger, more collaborative ecosystem to drive growth and create opportunity — a vision that sits close to IITG-TIC’s own work of helping ideas become sustainable, scalable ventures.

body.alt: The startup expo at mc² + IGNITE.
body.caption: The Startup Expo showcased solutions from emerging ventures.

body.text: PSUs, founders and industry

The participation of Oil India Limited and other energy-sector PSUs underlined the role industry plays in supporting startups — through real-world challenges, technology validation, pilot opportunities and deployment. At the Startup Expo, the Chief Minister met founders and explored their innovations directly.

body.alt: Panel discussion with founders at mc² + IGNITE.
body.caption: Founders from Quant Solar, MadVR Solutions and Ecoet Technologies in conversation.

body.text: A panel of founders from Quant Solar, MadVR Solutions and Ecoet Technologies discussed opportunities, challenges, investment, the role of incubators and pathways to scale. Prof. Ashok Jhunjhunwala of IIT Madras spoke on how startups and innovation can address India’s large, complex challenges, and Prof. Senthilmurugan Subbiah shared practical notes on founder commitment, product development and the work of incubation.
The response

With more than 1,500 participants, over 100 startups and around 1,000 students, the turnout reflected the growing entrepreneurial energy in the region. For IITG-TIC, mc² + IGNITE reaffirmed a simple commitment: nurture ideas, support founders, connect academia with industry, and help startups scale.

posts.title: Bharat Innovates 2026, Nice
posts.sliderTagline: Quant Solar on the global stage in Nice.
posts.excerpt: Quant Solar, an IITG-TIC incubated startup, represented India at Bharat Innovates in Nice, France — a global showcase of 120 startups across 13 frontier sectors.
posts.author: Quant Solar, incubated at IITG-TIC

coverImage.alt: The Quant Solar team at Bharat Innovates in Nice.

body.text: From the labs of IIT Guwahati to the global innovation stage: Quant Solar, an IITG Technology Incubation Centre (IITG-TIC) incubated startup, represented India’s innovation ecosystem at the inaugural edition of Bharat Innovates, held in Nice, France, from 14 to 16 June 2026 — a global showcase featuring 120 startups across 13 frontier sectors, selected from institutions across the country.
Research, ready for the world

Quant Solar’s presence reflected the growing strength of IIT Guwahati’s research and innovation ecosystem, and the readiness of its startups to compete internationally. At IITG-TIC, the work is to turn research into market-ready technologies that address global challenges in clean energy, climate resilience and sustainability.

body.alt: Quant Solar at the Bharat Innovates showcase.
body.caption: Quant Solar among 120 startups selected for the showcase.

body.text: Beyond the showcase

Bharat Innovates offered more than a stage. It opened conversations with European universities, research institutions, industry leaders, investors and policymakers — new avenues for technology validation, research collaboration, commercialisation and international market access.

body.alt: The Bharat Innovates gathering in Nice.
body.caption: Engaging with global universities, investors and industry in Nice.

body.text: Congratulations to the Quant Solar team on the milestone. It is the kind of moment IITG-TIC hopes to see repeated — more of its startups carrying Indian innovation to the world.

posts.title: AI-Assisted Coding Training Program
posts.sliderTagline: Five days of AI-assisted building at TIC.
posts.excerpt: A five-day intensive for professionals from Numaligarh Refinery Limited — from the fundamentals of AI-assisted development to hands-on product building with modern AI tools.
posts.author: IITG-TIC for Numaligarh Refinery Limited

coverImage.alt: Participants at the AI-Assisted Coding Training Program.

body.text: To equip professionals for a period in which AI is reshaping how we build and solve problems, IITG Technology Incubation Centre (IITG-TIC) ran an intensive five-day AI-Assisted Coding Training Program for participants from Numaligarh Refinery Limited.
Foundations, then building

The programme opened with an inaugural session and a talk by Urmi Buragohain on the innovation and incubation ecosystem. Early days covered the fundamentals of AI-assisted development, an introduction to large language models, and the shape of the evolving AI ecosystem. Participants then moved from concepts to creation — using tools such as Cursor AI and Claude Code for rapid prototyping and product development.

body.alt: A hands-on session during the training program.
body.caption: From concepts to creation — building AI-enabled products.

body.text: Data, machine learning and industry

Later sessions went deeper into the foundations. Prof. Senthilmurugan Subbiah led on data fundamentals, machine-learning concepts and preprocessing, and on the transformative role of AI in chemical engineering and process industries — industry use cases, process optimisation, and the importance of pairing AI with domain expertise. Prof. Neeraj Sharma introduced machine learning, deep learning, image processing and computer vision, and speech-processing technologies.

body.alt: A working session on the later days of the program.
body.caption: Deep-tech foundations, from data preprocessing to computer vision.

body.text: A session with Dr Geetha Manjunath — Founder, CEO and CTO of Niramai Health Analytix — traced her journey building a deep-tech healthcare startup and the role of innovation in creating impact. Across the week, participants left with a firmer grasp of both the theory and the practice of applying AI within their own domains.

posts.title: Battle Blitz 2026
posts.excerpt: A startup pitching competition at IITG-TIC — 20+ ideas from young founders across Assam, judged by a panel drawn from the region’s innovation ecosystem.
posts.author: IITG-TIC with Smile Foundation, Assam Startup and Apun NGO

coverImage.alt: Participants at the Battle Blitz pitching competition.

body.text: Battle Blitz 2026 — a startup pitching competition — was held at the Technology Incubation Centre, IIT Guwahati (IITG-TIC), organised together with the Smile Foundation, Assam Startup and Apun NGO. It brought a diverse, talented pool of participants into one room for an afternoon of ideas.
The pitches

More than twenty innovative ideas were pitched by students, startups and aspiring entrepreneurs from universities and colleges across Assam. The competition was a platform for creativity, entrepreneurial vision and problem-solving — a reflection of the region’s growing innovation ecosystem.

body.alt: A pitch in progress at Battle Blitz.
body.caption: Twenty-plus ideas from founders across Assam.

body.text: The jury

A distinguished panel evaluated the pitches: Trailukya Dutta, founder of Tholua Pratishthan, whose work centres on social impact and grassroots innovation; Kaushik Khanikar, consultant at Assam Startup, who supports emerging startups across the ecosystem; and Urmi Buragohain, CEO of the Technology Incubation Centre, IIT Guwahati.

body.alt: The audience and jury at Battle Blitz.
body.caption: Enthusiastic participation and high-quality pitches through the day.

body.text: Between the engaged discussions and the quality of the pitches, Battle Blitz 2026 stood as a marker of the momentum building around innovation and entrepreneurship in the region — with thanks to every participant, partner and jury member who made it work.

hero.intro: At IITG-TIC we don't just give you a desk and walk away. The centre is built around five connected forms of support — infrastructure, programme, technical depth, capital, and a place to live while you build. Each one exists to lower the cost of starting something hard, and shorten the distance between an idea and a paying customer.

links.title: Incubation Support
links.tagline: Launch your tech startup with in-house or digital incubation — workspace, labs, mentorship and a community that holds it together.

hero.lede: IITG-TIC offers two ways to incubate — a fully equipped in-house programme inside our campus, and a digital track for founders who can't be physically here. The support stays the same; the geography is yours to choose.

sections.label: In-house
paragraphs: Move into a fully equipped workstation inside the Technology Complex. Meeting rooms and shared spaces sit across the same building, so collaboration happens naturally rather than as a calendar invite.
Access state-of-the-art labs across electronics, biotechnology, machining and fabrication — the kind of equipment that turns a CAD file into a working prototype on the same week.
High-speed internet, IT infrastructure and the everyday plumbing that lets you focus on the work and forget the logistics.

image.alt: An in-house incubation workstation at the centre.

sections.label: Digital
paragraphs: Receive guidance from experienced mentors remotely, on the same cadence as our in-house cohort. Geography does not change the depth of the engagement.
Benefit from the programme's resources and structure on your own terms — no pressure to relocate, no compromise on what's offered.
Tap into a wider pool of investors and potential partners through our digital network. The door opens the same way; you just walk through it from wherever you are.

image.alt: A digital incubatee in a remote mentorship session.

sections.label: Community
paragraphs: Whether you're in-house or digital, you join a living community of fellow founders, mentors and industry experts. Some of the most valuable conversations happen in the margins of programmed time.

Cohort-wide events, peer reviews and informal exchanges form the connective tissue between incubatees. The community is small enough that everyone knows everyone — and serious enough that the conversations land.

image.alt: A cohort gathering at the centre's community space.

links.title: Infrastructure Support
links.tagline: Office space, shared facilities and access to IIT Guwahati's wider infrastructure — labs, library and expert opinion on call.

hero.lede: Infrastructure at IITG-TIC comes in three layers — your own office setup, shared facilities across the cohort, and access to the wider institute's labs, library and expert advisers when your work needs them.

sections.label: Individual setup
paragraphs: Office space is allocated against requirement — from a single desk to a private team room. Each setup includes a personal computer, internet connection and a working telephone line.
Office furniture is provided. On-campus accommodation is offered subject to availability — see our residence-support page if you'll need it.

image.alt: An allocated office setup at the centre.

sections.label: Shared facilities
paragraphs: A conference room equipped with projection equipment is available for cohort meetings, investor conversations and team workshops.
Shared office hardware — photocopier, fax machine, laser printer and scanner — is at every incubatee's disposal, so the small operational frictions don't become recurring problems.

sections.label: Institute resources
paragraphs: Incubatees can access the institute's wider infrastructure — labs, workshops and the IITG library — per the institute's standard norms.

Expert opinion on legal, financial and technical matters can be arranged from IITG faculty and advisers on a chargeable basis. Medical facilities at the institute are similarly available on chargeable terms.

image.alt: An incubatee using the IITG library.

links.title: Funding Support
links.tagline: Soft loans up to 80% of project cost, navigation across major government schemes, and CSR partnerships with corporates.

hero.lede: Funding at IITG-TIC comes through three connected paths — a soft-loan facility for selected incubatees, navigation help across major government schemes, and CSR partnerships with corporates who fund our work directly.

sections.label: Soft loan
paragraphs: IITG-TIC may offer a soft loan — entirely dependent on the availability of funds, grants and schemes meant for the purpose. We approach government, private and public-sector agencies for grants whenever the opportunity arises.

Soft loans are sanctioned only to registered companies. Admission to IITG-TIC does not automatically entitle a company to a loan, and disbursement follows the guidelines of the underlying funding agency.
The total loan available depends on the funding agency's criteria. As a guideline, soft loans cover up to 80% of project cost — with minimum simple interest where the underlying scheme permits.

sections.label: Government schemes
paragraphs: We help incubatees navigate the major schemes available to early-stage ventures — Startup India, the OIL India Fund and NEDFi Venture among them.
The documentation is half the battle. We've filed many of these before; the programme team will sit with you to assemble a serious application, not a hopeful one.

image.alt: A founder reviewing scheme paperwork at the centre.

sections.label: CSR partnerships
paragraphs: Section 135 of the Companies Act 2013 requires qualifying corporates to spend 2% of average net profits on Corporate Social Responsibility projects. Contributions to technology business incubators located within Central-Government-approved academic institutions qualify under Schedule VII, item (ix).

IITG-TIC is a non-profit technology business incubator hosted at IIT Guwahati since 2009 — one of the first in the North-East — supported by the Technology Development Board (TDB) and the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY). The centre runs across 15,000+ sq ft of infrastructure and has incubated ~19 companies to date.

Corporates can associate with IITG-TIC to implement projects in relevant technology areas, social innovation, or to fund the incubation programme directly. Write to inchargetic@iitg.ac.in or call +91 361 258 3191 to start a conversation.

image.alt: A corporate CSR partnership conversation in progress.

links.title: Technical Support
links.tagline: Labs, workshops and library access — plus faculty mentors and institute-grade testing facilities for product validation.

hero.lede: Our incubatees plug into the full technical depth of IIT Guwahati — the labs and workshops, the faculty who teach in them, and the institute-grade testing facilities that turn a prototype into a credible product.

sections.label: Labs & workshops
paragraphs: Incubatee companies are provided access to the laboratories and workshops of IIT Guwahati per the institute's standard norms — for everything from rapid fabrication to longer R&D cycles.

Mechanical, electronics, materials and embedded labs are routinely accessible. Specialised equipment — clean rooms, characterisation tools, fabrication facilities — is booked through the respective IITG departments based on availability.

image.alt: An incubatee using an IITG lab.

sections.label: Faculty mentors
paragraphs: Our mentors are faculty from IIT Guwahati. They provide full technical support — sitting in on architecture reviews, design reviews and code reviews as engineers, not as evaluators.

Mentor matches are made deliberately. A hardware founder is paired with someone who has built hardware; a software venture with someone who has shipped systems. The fit is the point of the match — not the title.
Beyond scheduled reviews, mentors are reachable for the small judgement calls that don't warrant a meeting but compound across a quarter.

image.alt: An IITG faculty mentor in a technical review.

sections.label: Testing facilities
paragraphs: Testing facilities at IIT Guwahati are available to incubatees — for product validation, performance characterisation, and the quality work that needs equipment beyond an early-stage budget.
Booking and access happen through the institute's standard channels. The programme team helps with introductions and the paperwork the first time you need them.
Use of the institute's library as a reference resource is included — particularly useful for deep-tech ventures that need access to journals, standards and technical literature.

image.alt: An incubatee running a product validation test.

links.title: Residence Support
links.tagline: Shared on-campus hostels inside IIT Guwahati — for founders who need to live close to the centre during a build cycle.

hero.lede: Some incubatees need to be physically close to the centre during a build cycle. Where possible, we offer residential space inside the IITG campus — shared hostels with basic amenities and proximity to the wider institute community.

sections.label: Shared hostels
paragraphs: Based on availability, startup teams are provided residential space with basic amenities in shared hostels on the IITG campus.
Rooms are furnished and utilities are included. Access to campus dining and the library follows the institute's standard norms.
Allocation is per team and per programme stage — not per founder. We aim to keep teams housed together so that the build doesn't lose its rhythm.

image.alt: A shared hostel room on the IITG campus.

sections.label: Campus life
paragraphs: The hostel sits inside the IITG campus, which means our incubatees live next door to the students. Some of the best conversations and recruiting moments happen because of that proximity.
Campus life includes access to dining halls, sports facilities, and academic events — the kind of environment that keeps founders close to fresh ideas and fresh hires.
It is, in practice, the closest thing we offer to building inside a research lab while still running a company.

image.alt: A view of campus life at IIT Guwahati.

sections.label: How to request
paragraphs: If you'll need residence support to join a cohort, mention it in your application — it helps us plan early and gives us time to confirm availability.
If the need arises mid-cohort, raise it with the programme manager. We respond within a week with a real answer — yes or no, with reasoning.

image.alt: A founder filling out a residence request form.

Our governing body, chaired by the Director of IIT Guwahati, sets the direction of the centre and keeps its work aligned with the wider mission of fostering deep-tech entrepreneurship in the North-East.

The questions we hear most often from founders, applicants and partners — and the straightest answers we can offer to each.

items.question: Who can apply to IITG-TIC?
items.answer: Anyone with a working idea and an inherent zeal to build a venture — students, faculty, alumni and outside founders are all welcome. We particularly encourage applicants from the North-East.

items.question: What kind of ideas does the centre support?
items.answer: Technology-led ideas — deep tech, hardware, software platforms, embedded systems, knowledge-based products. The idea should have a credible path to becoming a commercially viable venture.

items.question: What support does the centre provide?
items.answer: Workspace inside the Technology Complex, technical assistance, business mentoring, network access, and — subject to availability — a soft-loan facility.

items.question: Is funding available?
items.answer: Yes. Soft-loan support is available for qualifying incubatees, and we work with funding partners including the Technology Development Board and Startup India for further capital.

items.question: Do I need to be affiliated with IIT Guwahati?
items.answer: No. While we have a strong link with the IITG community, we welcome founders from anywhere — particularly from across the North-East ecosystem.

items.question: How long is the incubation programme?
items.answer: Programme length varies with the venture. Some incubatees graduate inside a year; others stay through multi-year R&D arcs. The arrangement is shaped to fit the work.

items.question: How do I apply?
items.answer: Head to the Apply page and submit your idea. Our team will review it and reach out for a conversation if it looks like a fit.

whatHappens.title: What Happens at TIC · IITG TIC

hero.lede: A home for new-age entrepreneurs and young minds to transform innovative ideas into viable business ventures — with mentorship, infrastructure, and a multidisciplinary push from IIT Guwahati and the wider North-East ecosystem.

sections.label: Who We Are
paragraphs: The Indian Institute of Technology Guwahati — Technology Incubation Centre (IITG-TIC) is a space for new-age entrepreneurs and young minds to transform their innovative ideas into viable business propositions. Our primary goal is to facilitate a platform where a budding entrepreneur can start a business venture with minimum risks.

IITG-TIC ensures that incubatees have access to technological assistance, generated through mentors with multidisciplinary expertise. We encourage young enthusiasts — those with creative pursuits and an inherent zeal to be entrepreneurs — to take advantage of this novel initiative.

callout.text: Curious about the people who keep this space alive? Come say hello to the team that powers it every day.
callout.label: Meet the TIC Team

sections.label: Our Mission
paragraphs: IITG-TIC is registered as a Society under the Registration of Societies Act XXI of 1860. Its goal is to encourage entrepreneurial initiatives amongst the faculty and alumni of the IITG community in particular — and other State or Central Government technical institutions of the North-East more broadly. It is an opportunity to explore and implement innovative ideas into commercially viable products through technology startup companies.

The centre facilitates interdisciplinary research with special emphasis on the development and innovation of high-growth, knowledge-based businesses — and nurtures indigenous products with innovative hardware and embedded designs.

callout.text: This mission only moves because of the mentors who walk alongside our founders. Take a moment to meet the people who carry it forward.
callout.label: Meet our Mentors

sections.label: Infrastructure & Support
paragraphs: Technical support, business mentoring, and a soft-loan facility — subject to availability — are the key services of this centre. Spreading across an area of approximately 4,000 square metres within the Technology Complex of IIT Guwahati, IITG-TIC has the adequate infrastructure for this endeavour.

Funds for developing basic infrastructure and the soft-loan facility are provided by the Department of Information Technology, Govt. of India. IITG-TIC is also one of the Business Incubators approved and recognised by the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Govt. of India. The Technology Development Board, under the Ministry of Science & Technology, has additionally approved grant assistance to IITG-TIC to support startup units.

callout.text: Wondering what working out of this space actually looks like? Take a closer look at our incubation programmes and the support we offer.
callout.label: Explore Incubation

sections.label: Governance
paragraphs: IITG-TIC has a ten-member Governing Body under the Chairmanship of the Director of IIT Guwahati. A Management Council directs and administers the smooth functioning of the centre. Currently, the Management Team of the IITG-TIC is led by a Chief Executive Officer.

callout.text: Want to know who steers all of this? Get to know the Governing Body that shapes the centre's direction.
callout.label: Meet the Governing Body

hero.headlineEmphasis: programmes a founder here can use.

schemesFunding.emptyMessage: No funding schemes are listed right now. Write to tic@iitg.ac.in and the team will point you to what is currently open.

schemes.label: GENESIS · EiR
schemes.name: MeitY GENESIS — Entrepreneur-in-Residence (EiR) Support
schemes.tagline: Idea-stage funding for first-time, first-generation entrepreneurs from Tier-II and Tier-III India.
schemes.description: GENESIS (Gen-Next Support for Innovative Startups) is a Government of India scheme run by MeitY Startup Hub to discover and fund technology startups outside metro cities. Its EiR vertical is built specifically for individuals at the ideation or validation stage who haven't yet raised significant funding. IITG-TIC is an implementing partner for this scheme in the North East.
schemes.amount: Up to ₹10 Lakh in equity-free support, released in milestone-based tranches.
eligibility: First-generation entrepreneurs, 18 years or older
Founders working full-time on their startup idea
Startups with total prior external funding (including government grants) under ₹10 Lakh
Applicants from Tier-II/Tier-III cities — Guwahati and the wider North East qualify
Focus areas: Electronics Design & Manufacturing, ICT, and Deep-Tech Software & Products

schemes.label: GENESIS · Pilot
schemes.name: MeitY GENESIS — Pilot (Proof-of-Concept) Support
schemes.tagline: Funding to prove your product works with a real industry or PSU partner.
schemes.description: The Pilot vertical of GENESIS helps startups validate their solution through a structured pilot project with a corporate, PSU, or large enterprise partner — turning a working prototype into a market-tested product with a credible reference customer.
schemes.amount: Average ₹40 Lakh, up to a maximum of ₹50 Lakh per startup.
eligibility: Startups with a working prototype ready for real-world pilot testing
Teams targeting corporate, PSU, or enterprise customers
Sectors: IT & AI, Electronics Design & Manufacturing, Deep-Tech, and related ICT domains
help: Helps identify and approach suitable pilot partners
Supports the pilot funding application and documentation
Provides technical validation support from IIT Guwahati labs during the pilot

schemes.label: GENESIS · Matching
schemes.name: MeitY GENESIS — Matching Investment Support
schemes.tagline: Co-investment support once you have a private investor on board.
schemes.description: For startups that have secured commitment from a private investor, GENESIS matches that investment 1:1, effectively doubling the capital available for commercialisation and scale-up — without diluting founders further than the original round.
schemes.amount: Average ₹40 Lakh, up to ₹50 Lakh, matched 1:1 against private investment.
eligibility: Startups with a confirmed private investor commitment
Deep-tech, ICT, or electronics-focused ventures
Companies ready to deploy capital toward market entry and scaling

schemes.label: SISFS
schemes.name: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS)
schemes.tagline: DPIIT's national seed fund for proof of concept through to commercialisation.
schemes.description: SISFS is the Government of India's flagship seed funding scheme, disbursed through DPIIT-recognised incubators such as IITG-TIC. It covers two distinct needs: validating your product and taking it to market.
schemes.amount: Up to ₹20 Lakh as a grant for proof of concept, prototyping, or product trials, plus up to ₹50 Lakh as investment (via convertible debentures or debt-linked instruments) for market entry and scaling.
eligibility: Startups recognised by DPIIT, incorporated within the last 2 years
Technology-driven businesses solving a clear problem with scalable potential
Priority sectors: social impact, waste management, financial inclusion, education, agriculture, healthcare, and more

schemes.label: Assam & state grants
schemes.name: Assam Startup & State Government Grants
schemes.tagline: State-level support layered on top of central government schemes.
schemes.description: Through our partnership with the Assam Startup Mission (AISF) and other state bodies, IITG-TIC helps North East-based founders access state grants, subsidies, and policy benefits designed specifically for startups registered or operating in Assam — often stackable with central schemes like GENESIS or SISFS.
schemes.amount: Varies by scheme; confirm current grant slabs with the IITG-TIC funding desk.
eligibility: Startups registered or headquartered in Assam
Founders looking to combine state and central government funding
Ventures in state-prioritised sectors (agritech, handloom-tech, tourism-tech, and more)

schemes.label: Soft loan
schemes.name: IITG-TIC Soft Loan Support
schemes.tagline: Bridge financing when grant disbursement timelines don't match your working-capital needs.
schemes.description: Where funds are available under relevant grants and schemes, IITG-TIC facilitates soft loans to incubated startups — low-interest bridge financing to cover working capital gaps between milestone-based grant disbursements.
schemes.amount: Subject to availability of funds, grants, and schemes designated for this purpose at the time of application.
eligibility: Actively incubated IITG-TIC startups facing a short-term capital gap
Startups with an approved grant pending milestone-based disbursement

schemes.label: iDEX-DIO
schemes.name: iDEX-DIO — Defence Innovation Support
schemes.tagline: Innovation and funding support for startups developing technology solutions for the Indian defence sector.
schemes.description: iDEX (Innovations for Defence Excellence) is a Government of India initiative implemented through the Defence Innovation Organisation (DIO) to promote innovation and technology development in the defence sector. IITG-TIC supports startups and innovators in accessing iDEX opportunities, challenges, mentorship, and funding.
schemes.amount: Funding varies by challenge. iDEX opportunities may provide grants of up to ₹1.5 Crore under DISC and significantly higher support under selected ADITI challenges.
eligibility: Startups, innovators, and technology developers working on defence solutions
Startups developing indigenous and innovative technologies
Solutions addressing specific defence requirements and challenge statements
Applicants from technology areas including drones, AI, robotics, defence electronics, advanced materials, cybersecurity, and other deep-tech domains

schemes.label: OIL SNEH
schemes.name: OIL SNEH — CSR-Supported Entrepreneurship Program
schemes.tagline: CSR-supported innovation and entrepreneurship development for aspiring entrepreneurs and startups in the North East.
schemes.description: OIL SNEH is a CSR initiative supported by Oil India Limited (OIL) aimed at promoting entrepreneurship, innovation, and livelihood opportunities. The program provides structured support to aspiring entrepreneurs and innovators through capacity building, mentoring, and ecosystem support.
schemes.amount: Training, mentoring, entrepreneurship development, innovation support, and ecosystem engagement, depending on the program component.
eligibility: Aspiring entrepreneurs and innovators
Early-stage entrepreneurs and startups
Participants from the North Eastern region
Individuals seeking support to develop and validate innovative business ideas

schemes.label: NRL Ideathon
schemes.name: NRL Ideathon — Innovation & Entrepreneurship Program
schemes.tagline: Ideation platform for discovering innovative solutions to real-world industry and societal challenges.
schemes.description: The NRL Ideathon is an innovation-focused initiative supported by Numaligarh Refinery Limited (NRL) to identify promising ideas and encourage entrepreneurship among students, innovators, and aspiring founders. The program provides a platform for participants to develop and present technology-driven solutions.
schemes.amount: Idea evaluation, mentoring, innovation guidance, industry exposure, and opportunities for further development of promising solutions.
eligibility: Students and young innovators
Aspiring entrepreneurs and startup founders
Technology and engineering teams
Participants developing solutions for industrial, energy, sustainability, and societal challenges

schemes.label: FICCI CSR
schemes.name: FICCI India — CSR Entrepreneurship Program
schemes.tagline: CSR-supported entrepreneurship and innovation development for emerging innovators and startups in the North East.
schemes.description: The FICCI India CSR Program supports entrepreneurship and innovation through structured capacity building, mentoring, and incubation support. The program helps promising innovators strengthen their ideas, develop entrepreneurial capabilities, and connect with the startup ecosystem.
schemes.amount: Entrepreneurship training, mentoring, business development support, ecosystem exposure, and incubation opportunities.
eligibility: Aspiring entrepreneurs and innovators
Early-stage startups and idea-stage founders
Entrepreneurs from the North Eastern region
Individuals developing innovative and technology-enabled solutions

schemes.label: GENESIS · Investment
schemes.name: MeitY GENESIS — Investment Component
schemes.tagline: Equity investment support for promising technology startups through a 1:1 matching investment model.
schemes.description: GENESIS (Gen-Next Support for Innovative Startups) is a Government of India initiative implemented by MeitY Startup Hub to strengthen the startup ecosystem beyond major metropolitan cities. Under the Investment Component, selected startups can receive matching equity investment through their incubator, helping them raise follow-on capital and accelerate growth. IITG-TIC is an implementing partner for GENESIS in the North East.
schemes.amount: Up to ₹40 Lakh in matching investment support, subject to the applicable GENESIS guidelines and investor contribution.
eligibility: Technology-driven startups with a scalable business model
Startups seeking early-stage equity investment
Startups with potential for growth, market adoption, and follow-on funding
Startups meeting the eligibility criteria under the GENESIS Investment Component
Startups from Tier-II/Tier-III cities and emerging startup ecosystems, including the North East
Focus areas include Deep-Tech, AI/ML, Electronics, ICT, and other technology-driven products and solutions

schemes.label: GENESIS · Deep-Tech
schemes.name: MeitY GENESIS — Deep-Tech Funding Support
schemes.tagline: Funding support for selected startups developing high-impact, technology-driven solutions.
schemes.description: MeitY GENESIS provides funding and ecosystem support to selected startups working on innovative and high-impact technology solutions. The program aims to help promising startups validate their technology, strengthen product development, and accelerate commercialization.
schemes.amount: Funding support is provided to a select number of eligible startups, based on the applicable GENESIS component, evaluation, and milestone requirements.
eligibility: Technology-driven startups developing high-impact solutions
Early-stage startups with innovative and scalable technologies
Startups working on deep-tech and emerging technology areas
Founders developing solutions with strong market and societal impact
Startups meeting the eligibility and selection criteria under the MeitY GENESIS program
